description:
What an unforgettable night it was for Mats Sundin. In his quest for three goals to reach the coveted 500-goal milestone in his career, he did so with remarkable flair, achieving a sensational hat trick, with the milestone goal occurring during overtime while his team was shorthanded. Sundin's first goal of the evening came in the opening period when Bryan McCabe spotted him open on the left side, setting up a perfect one-timer. Late in the second period, with the score knotted at three, Sundin showcased his prowess by launching a snap shot from the right side, beating the opposing goaltender for his second goal of the game. Then, in the thrilling overtime period, while his team was down a player, Sundin carried the puck over the blue line and unleashed a blistering slap shot that found the top shelf of the net, igniting an ecstatic frenzy among the Toronto crowd. Sundin's illustrious career saw him amass a total of 1,349 points, with a remarkable 987 of those points earned while donning the Toronto Maple Leafs jersey, securing his place at the top of the all-time list for the franchise.

description:
Alec Martinez earned three Stanley Cups during his time with the Los Angeles Kings, but the 2014 Stanley Cup was particularly memorable for him. He scored the series-clinching goal in the second overtime of Game 5 of the Stanley Cup Final. Amid chants of "We want the Cup" from the home crowd during a Kings' offensive rush, Martinez capitalized on a rebound from an initial save, firing the puck into the open net for the decisive goal. The arena erupted in celebration, with Martinez, his teammates, and the entire Los Angeles crowd sharing in the jubilation. Of the five goals Martinez scored in the 2014 playoffs, three were game winners including two in overtime.

description:
In his quest for 1,000 career points, Daniel Alfredsson achieved this milestone in spectacular fashion, notching a memorable hat trick that included the game-winning goal. In the first period, Alfredsson was the first player to grace the scoresheet, redirecting a shot from Erik Karlsson at the point during a power play. Then, midway through the second period, with the score deadlocked at two, Alfredsson capitalized on a Buffalo turnover in the neutral zone, gaining control of the puck and embarking on a two-on-one rush. Faced with a Buffalo defender who denied the passing option, Alfredsson unleashed a half-clapper that sailed past the opposing netminder, securing the eventual game-winning goal. Finally, to clinch his 1,000th point, Alfredsson sealed the victory for the Senators in the waning moments of the game, sending a backhander into the empty net, securing a 4-2 triumph. Out of Alfredsson's impressive 1,157 career points, a staggering 1,108 were earned during his tenure as a member of the Ottawa Senators – a franchise with whom he spent 17 of his 18 NHL seasons. Alfredsson's contributions with the Senators place him atop the franchise’s all-time points list, with an astounding 421-point lead on the club’s next highest-scoring player, Jason Spezza.

description:
In his 19th NHL season, all spent with the Pittsburgh Penguins, Evgeni Malkin reached a historic milestone by scoring his 500th career goal. With a Penguins power play just expired, Malkin broke toward the net and received a crisp pass from Sidney Crosby, stationed below the goal line. Although his initial attempt was stopped, Malkin's determination paid off as he slammed the rebound home while sprawled on the ice. Finishing the game with one goal and three assists, Malkin delivered a memorable performance in front of an electrified home crowd. At the time of the milestone, he ranked third in both goals and points in the storied history of the Penguins franchise.

description:
In 2017, Corey Perry became the third player in NHL history—and the first since Maurice “Rocket” Richard in 1951—to score three overtime goals in a single playoff season. After sweeping the Calgary Flames in the Western Conference First Round, where Perry netted the Game 3 overtime winner, the Anaheim Ducks faced the Edmonton Oilers in the Second Round. With the series tied, Perry struck again in double overtime of a pivotal Game 5. After receiving a pass in the slot, Perry skated in, partially freezing the goalie, then patiently maneuvered around the outstretched leg to tuck the puck into the far side of the net. The former Hart Trophy and Stanley Cup winner would go on to score his third overtime goal in the following series against Nashville.

description:
Throughout NHL history, some of the most memorable goalie performances have come from a consistent "body of work," where a netminder wins a game or series despite being heavily outplayed, making crucial saves at key moments. But every so often, a single save stands out as both pivotal and breathtaking. Such was the case in Game 2 of the 2018 Stanley Cup Final. With the Capitals clinging to a one-goal lead and under two minutes left, Braden Holtby made an incredible diving save with the paddle of his stick, robbing Alex Tuch of what seemed like a sure goal into an open net. Holtby’s save helped Washington even the series on the road and sparked the Capitals' run of four straight wins to capture their first-ever Stanley Cup championship.

description:
Sergei Bobrovsky made NHL history as the fastest goaltender to reach 400 career wins, becoming just the 14th netminder to achieve this milestone. Bobrovsky accomplished the feat in only 707 games, surpassing the previous record held by Henrik Lundqvist by 20 games.  
In his milestone victory against the New York Rangers, Bobrovsky delivered a standout performance with several clutch saves. During a Rangers power play in the first period, he denied Chris Kreider twice from point-blank range at the doorstep. In the second period, Bobrovsky silenced the New York crowd once again with a stunning sequence: he stopped a dangerous wrist shot from Braden Schneider in the slot and immediately followed it up with a right-pad save on Vincent Trocheck’s close-range rebound attempt.  
Already a Stanley Cup champion and two-time Vezina Trophy winner, Bobrovsky continues to add remarkable achievements to his illustrious career.

description:
In the 2012 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Philadelphia Flyers faced off against their rival, the Pittsburgh Penguins, a team they hadn’t beaten in a playoff series since 2000. With a chance to clinch the series in Game 6, Flyers captain Claude Giroux made an immediate impact. Right after the opening faceoff, Giroux delivered a massive hit on Sidney Crosby, igniting the home crowd. Moments later, in the same shift, he fired in the first goal, giving the Flyers a lead they never surrendered as they went on to eliminate the Penguins. Giroux dominated the series, leading all players with 14 points in six games. Throughout the decade beginning with the 2010-11 season, Giroux ranked 4th in the league for points and was a Top 5 finalist for the Hart Trophy in three different seasons.

description:

Kopitar was a standout during the 2012 Stanley Cup Playoffs, tying for the league lead in goals (8), assists (12), and points (20).

description:
In his final season with the Chicago Blackhawks, where he spent the first 15 years of his NHL career, Bobby Hull reached the historic 600-goal milestone with his signature blistering slap shot. The goal, set up by a pass from his brother Dennis Hull, tied the game late in the third period and made Hull just the second player in NHL history, after Gordie Howe, to achieve the feat. A two-time Hart Trophy winner and three-time Art Ross Trophy recipient, Hull also won a Stanley Cup with Chicago and remains the franchise’s all-time leader in goals.

description:
In his 601st career start, Carey Price stood on the brink of hockey history, needing just one win to surpass the legendary Jacques Plante as the Montreal Canadiens' all-time leader in victories. The stage was set at the Bell Centre, where Price would deliver an extraordinary performance, making a series of crucial saves throughout the night. Early in the game, Price was tested as Andreas Athanasiou found himself on a breakaway, but the Canadiens' netminder stood tall, denying the scoring opportunity. In the second period, with the game still scoreless, Price showcased his brilliance by stopping a shot from the point followed up by an exceptional pad save on the rebound, denying the opposition a valuable lead. When another Detroit Red Wings breakaway threatened, Price came up with a jaw-dropping left pad save, frustrating Tyler Bertuzzi's deke attempt and preserving his team's chances. When the final buzzer sounded, Price had made 20 saves on 21 shots, securing his 315th career victory and etching his name in Canadiens history as the franchise's all-time wins leader.

description:
In the 1970s, Phil Esposito reigned supreme as the NHL’s top goal-scorer, and his record-breaking feats set him apart from the pack. In the 1970-71 season, Esposito made history by shattering Bobby Hull's single-season goals record, scoring his 59th goal on March 11, 1971, against the Los Angeles Kings. With a perfect redirect off Ted Green's shot, Esposito surpassed Hull’s mark and continued to add to his total, finishing the season as the first player to reach an astonishing 76 goals. Esposito’s 152-point performance in 1970-71 also set a record at the time, and he remains in elite company as one of only five different players in NHL history to hit that benchmark. Dominating the League as a six-time NHL goals leader, Esposito’s offensive prowess propelled the Bruins to two Stanley Cup victories (1970 and 1972) and earned him five Art Ross Trophies as NHL points leader, along with two Hart Trophies as MVP.

Kane one-timed the puck into the net, sealing the Blackhawks' third championship in six seasons and sending the home crowd into a frenzy. Kane finished the 2015 playoffs tied for the lead in points with 23.

description:
After trailing three games to one in their Western Conference Semifinals series against the Detroit Red Wings, the Chicago Blackhawks won back-to-back games to force a decisive Game 7 at home. Tied 1-1, the game went into overtime. As play unfolded along the boards, the puck found its way to Brent Seabrook, who skated through open ice, carried it across the blue line, and unleashed a wrist shot from the top of the circles. The shot deflected off a defender and past the goaltender for the game winner. Chicago went on to win the Stanley Cup that year, defeating the Boston Bruins.

description:
With just nine seconds left on the clock, Filip Gustavsson etched his name in NHL history, becoming the 15th goaltender ever credited with a goal. After gloving down a neutral-zone slap shot from the Blues, the Wild netminder wasted no time. He dropped the puck to his stick, dropped to one knee, and launched a high, arcing shot the length of the ice. It landed perfectly in the offensive zone and rolled into the empty net, sealing a 4-1 victory. His teammates on the ice immediately swarmed Gustavsson to celebrate the unforgettable moment.

description:
On February 11, 2017, Henrik Lundqvist joined an elite group of NHL goaltenders as he notched his 400th career win. On that memorable night, Lundqvist showcased his exceptional skills by making a series of outstanding saves, ultimately securing the victory with an impressive performance of 32 saves on 34 shots. His stellar play earned him “First Star of the Game” honors.  The Madison Square Garden faithful passionately supported their beloved goaltender with resounding "Henrik" chants throughout the third period and at the conclusion of the match. As of now, Lundqvist stands as the sixth-winningest goaltender in NHL history and holds the New York Rangers franchise mark for career victories.

description:
Nathan MacKinnon made history at home against the Chicago Blackhawks, becoming the 100th player to join the prestigious 1,000-point club. Reaching the milestone in just his 856th career game, he became the fourth-fastest among all active players to achieve the feat. Battling for the puck in the corner, MacKinnon emerged with possession, skated around the net, and fed it to Devon Toews at the point. Toews’ shot was tipped in by Artturi Lehkonen, earning MacKinnon his milestone point. He later added another assist, finishing with two points in the Avalanche’s victory.
